title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a field of finite type over Q (the 'base' B_K, viewed via its étale topos / Galois groupoid Π_K). Choosing an algebraic closure K̄ gives the absolute Galois group E_{K̄/K}, the induced algebraic closure Q̄ inside K̄, and a restriction homomorphism (7) E_{K̄/K} → Γ_{Q̄/Q} = Gal(Q̄/Q). On the previous page Grothendieck calls the kernel π_{K̄/K} the 'geometric part' and the image Γ_{K̄/K} the 'arithmetic part'.

On this page he identifies the image. It is an open subgroup of Gal(Q̄/Q). It corresponds to the finite extension K_0 = algebraic closure of Q in K, so Γ_{K̄/K} = Gal(Q̄/K_0). This gives the exact sequence
(8) 1 → π_{K̄/K} → E_{K̄/K} → Γ_{K̄/K} → 1, with Γ_{K̄/K} ↪ Γ_{Q̄/Q}.
In modern terms π_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/KQ̄) is the absolute Galois group of the 'geometric' function field KQ̄ over Q̄. A marginal note adds: π_{K̄/K} = 1 iff K is algebraic over Q, i.e. (K being of finite type) finite over Q.

To interpret (8) he writes (9) K = colim A_i, the directed union of finitely generated Q-subalgebras A_i ⊂ K. Equivalently Spec K = lim U_i over the projective system of affine models U_i = Spec A_i of K/Q. In characteristic 0 (generic smoothness) the regular A_i, i.e. U_i smooth over Q, form a cofinal subsystem. One may even take transition maps to be localizations A_i → (A_i)_{f_ij} with f_ij ≠ 0, so that the U_j ↪ U_i are open immersions; this works by taking a common denominator.

The next page continues: E_{K̄/K} = lim π_1(U_i), each with a homotopy exact sequence 1 → π_1(Ū_i) → π_1(U_i) → Gal(Q̄/K_0) → 1. Passing to the limit expresses π_{K̄/K} as lim π_1(U_i ⊗ Q̄). This is the standard set-up for 'birational' anabelian geometry and the Galois action on geometric fundamental groups.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor implicit hypothesis: the 'i.e. fini sur Q' in the NB, and the finiteness of K_0/Q, require K to be of finite type over Q (assumed throughout).
Surjectivity of E_{K̄/K} → Gal(Q̄/K_0) uses that K_0 is algebraically closed in K, hence K and Q̄ are linearly disjoint over K_0 (char 0). This is not stated but is standard.

The claim that transition maps can be taken to be localizations holds only for a cofinal subsystem (localizations of one smooth model A_0), not for the full system of all finitely generated subalgebras.

ideas.what: Splitting the absolute Galois group of a finitely generated field over Q into geometric part Gal(K̄/KQ̄) and arithmetic part Gal(Q̄/K_0) via an exact sequence
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental (arithmetic–geometric) exact sequence for function fields; birational anabelian setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1 homotopy exact sequence; birational anabelian programme), later Pop, Neukirch–Uchida–Ikeda for the anabelian results
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX–X (homotopy exact sequence); Esquisse d'un programme and letter to Faltings (1983) for the anabelian/birational viewpoint

ideas.what: Field of finite type as limit of its smooth affine models with open-immersion transition maps; Galois group as limit of fundamental groups of models
ideas.modern_name: Generic point as a limit of models; π_1 commutes with cofiltered limits of schemes with affine transitions
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §8; SGA1 Exp. V; SGA4 VII

ideas.what: Criterion: geometric part trivial iff K algebraic over Q
ideas.modern_name: Elementary fact on absolute Galois groups of function fields

deep.surprise_reason: Standard expository set-up (fundamental exact sequence for a function field, limit over smooth models) leading into the birational/anabelian discussion of the Longue Marche. Nothing beyond well-known material.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 '[qui], de la sorte' is unclear; the sense is 'qui, en tant que tel, correspond à un sous-corps K_0'. Reading uncertain.
The image of (8) shows the quotient Γ_{K̄/K} with a vertical arrow ↪ Γ_{Q̄/Q} below it. This matches the transcription, but in the margin of the previous page the same group is written Γ'.
The marginal NB (written diagonally) reads roughly 'NB π_{K̄/K} = (1) ssi K alg. sur Q, i.e. fini sur Q'.
'i.e. les U_i lisses /Q' is an interlinear insertion above 'avec comme morphismes de transition'.
